r.정치 구도: The 1987 constitution set up a system in which the president and the prime minister share power, but today Haiti has no elected officials at the national level. Elections kept being postponed after the president was assassinated at his home in July 2021, and in January 2023 the terms of the last senators ran out. In April 2024 nine representatives of parties and civic groups formed a Transitional Presidential Council, but amid infighting and corruption allegations its term ended on 7 February 2026, and since then the prime minister has led the government. In 2024 the gangs formed a coalition called Viv Ansanm that took over most of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and at times shut down the airport, the port and main roads. The government has said it will hold elections in 2026, but insecurity keeps pushing the date back.

t.why: Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean with the Dominican Republic and won independence from France through a slave revolution in 1804. In 1825 it agreed to pay France a huge indemnity in return for recognition and spent decades paying it off, a debt often cited as one of the roots of its poverty. After the 2010 earthquake killed hundreds of thousands of people, UN peacekeepers and international aid poured in, but the state never got back on its feet. A Kenyan-led multinational security support mission arrived in 2024, and in 2025 the UN Security Council decided to turn it into a 5,500-strong Gang Suppression Force. Troops began arriving in April 2026, but only about 2,000 had deployed by October, and the Council extended the mission to March 2027. So many people have fled their homes because of the gangs that Haiti is also a constant in news about migration policy in the Dominican Republic and the United States.
t.rel: It shares an island with the Dominican Republic. Gangs control most of the capital and security has collapsed; a UN-authorized foreign security support mission is deployed there.
t.korea: The two countries established diplomatic relations in September 1962. Right after the January 2010 earthquake South Korea sent a rescue team, and from February 2010 to December 2012 the Danbi Unit served as UN peacekeepers in Léogâne, clearing rubble, building roads and providing medical care. Even before the earthquake, Korean-run garment factories accounted for a large share of Haiti's exports. In October 2012 Sae-A Trading, together with the US government and the Inter-American Development Bank, opened a clothing factory in the Caracol Industrial Park in the north; before COVID-19 it employed 12,000 people, the park's largest employer. In recent years, though, it has let thousands of workers go.
t.know: Haiti won independence through a slave revolt in 1804, becoming the first republic founded by Black people.
etext: Money sent home by Haitians in the United States, Canada and the Dominican Republic is a pillar of the economy, worth around a fifth of GDP.
Most exports are clothing bound for the United States. US tariff preferences for Haitian-made apparel are what brought the factories in.
Haiti sells mangoes, coffee and cocoa, and it is one of the world's leading producers of vetiver oil, used in perfume.

Gangs block roads and the port so goods cannot move on time, and the economy has shrunk for several years in a row. Heavy deforestation leaves it exposed to floods and landslides, and the power supply is unreliable.
